chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluwayh (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Isa al-Ubaydi, from Abu Zakariyya the believer, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him). He said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him and his family) came to some youth from the Ansar and said: I want to recite to you, so whoever weeps will have Paradise.
He recited the end of [Surat] al-Zumar, "Those who disbelieve will be driven to Hell in groups" [39:71] to the end of the chapter.

The whole community wept except one youth. He said: O Messenger of Allah! I tried to weep, but my eyes shed no tears. He said: I will repeat it to you, and whoever tries to weep will have Paradise. So he repeated it to them, and the community wept and the youth tried to weep, and they all entered Paradise.

key_terms.الأنصار: The Ansar: the Muslims of Medina who received and supported the Prophet and his companions upon the Hijra
key_terms.الزمر: Surah al-Zumar (chapter 39 of the Quran), meaning 'The Groups/Crowds', describing the scenes of the Day of Judgment
key_terms.تَبَاكَى: To force oneself to weep or try hard to weep (taba'ka); a voluntary effort to achieve the emotional state of weeping

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about weeping while listening to the Quran?
ai.summary: This narrative from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) describes the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) reciting the concluding verses of Surah al-Zumar to a group of Ansar youth, promising Paradise to those who weep. When one youth could not shed tears despite his sincere effort (taba'ka), the Prophet mercifully extended the promise to those who sincerely try to weep, then repeated the recitation so all would be included. This hadith establishes that sincere emotional engagement with the Quran — even striving to weep without succeeding — is meritorious and carries the promise of Paradise.
